To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We present a new algorithm for computing the product of two polynomials of degree at most \(d\) in \(\mathcal{O}\bigl (\min\{N^{2}\log ^{2}d, N^{2}\log d, N^{3}\log d, d^{\omega }\log d\}\bigr )\) time and \(\mathcal {O}(N\log d)\) space.

(i) the evaluation of multivariate polynomials in the ring of RLWE encryption is more efficient than the evaluation of univariate polynomials, and (ii) the evaluation of low degree multivariate polynomials is even more efficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficient evaluation of multivariate polynomials in ring-LWE homomorphic encryption schemes.
the evaluation of ring polynomials of degree \(d\).
the efficient evaluation of low degree multivariate polynomials over encrypted ring data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the more coefficients of the polynomial that are used to encrypt data, the more complex the computations become.

, for the use cases of homomorphically encrypted data that only use the \(\text{degree-}0 \) coefficient of the polynomial, the evaluation of low degree multivariate polynomials can be performed efficiently.

, for the use cases where only degree-0 coefficient is used for encryption, the proposed scheme is more efficient than the existing one, and for the cases where more than one coefficient is used, the existing one is more efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to efficiently perform generic computations when the degree of the polynomial used for the encryption is low.
we provide an efficient way to evaluate a low-degree multivariate polynomial over encrypted data in ring-LWE homomorphic encryption schemes.
we have shown how to perform generic computations on ring-LWE ciphertexts with a single degree-1 coefficient and a single degree-0 coefficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in such cases, it is possible to evaluate low-degree multivariate polynomials over encrypted data in an efficient manner.
the evaluation of low degree multivariate polynomials is more efficient than the evaluation of univariate polynomials.
in this case it is possible to use the same number of coefficients as for degree-0 only computations.
